text.p: Norwegian power producer Hafslund ASA is expected to book profits before tax of 310 million crowns for the full-year 1996, a Reuter survey of eight Norwegian and foreign analysts showed.
For the corresponding year ago period, the company posted pre-tax profits of 341 million crowns.
Two of the analysts recommended to buy the share, three said hold and one said sell. Two experts declined to provide a recommendation.
Several of the analysts said Hafslund was a good "insurance element" in a share portfolio.

"Hafslund should be at the bottom of every portfolio. If the bourse should fall back slightly -- and that's not improbable -- Hafslund would be a good shelter because it will be stable in periods of downturn," said one of the analysts.
Others were disappointed Hafslund had been slow to expand via buyouts of other power companies following the demerger with drug group Nycomed in 1996.
However, most of the analysts said Hafslund had good potential in the long term, especially now Sweden had decided to phase out nuclear power stations.
"Hafslund, with its hydropower, will become very interesting in the long term. In the near-term picture, however, it is dull," said another analyst.
